_note: TEMPLATE. opencode.json is GENERATED from this file at every start (by the app's agent-cfg crate, which also drops every `_` key): edit here, never there. The values in double curly braces come from mango-models.json.
_model: GENERATED: the app's default model. Both entries are left out while no model is on the computer.
_small_model: The same provider and model as the running one: with a cloud model the session title and summaries would look for another provider and fail with an authentication error.

mango.name: mango-code
mango._baseURL: GENERATED: normally http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, but with the engine of another PC it is that PC's address.
mango._options: apiKey is fake but MUST be there (the OpenAI-compatible client refuses to start without it). timeout false and headerTimeout 15 min are needed: a 50k-token prefill can take two minutes before the first byte, and the default 30-60 s would cut the request on long contexts.

local._local: GENERATED: this entry becomes one per model the app declares, each with its own name, attachment, modalities and limit.
local._modalities: GENERATED: [text, image] if the model has an mmproj. REQUIRED, not a duplicate of `attachment`: without it opencode does not send the images a tool returns (a screenshot) and puts an 'ERROR: Cannot read image' message in their place (capabilities.input.image comes from modalities.input, not from attachment).
local._variants: No variants: the model always reasons, and without variants the web UI shows no selector next to the model.

_compaction: prune false: pruning old tool outputs changes the old part of the conversation and the engine re-reads everything after it. Auto compaction summarizes once when the context is full.
_plugin: Normally empty: the plugins in the plugin folder next to this file load by themselves. Filled only for the Team manager, whose config folder is elsewhere, with absolute paths (for the dev it would load the plugin twice).
_timeout_30s: A short timeout, not the 120000 ms default: the stdio channel to an MCP server can die silently, and only the client giving up quickly makes the model notice within two calls. The server's protocolTimeout (20 s) must stay BELOW this one.
_why_node_not_npx: chrome-devtools-mcp is launched with `node` on the mango-chrome-mcp.mjs wrapper, not with `npx`: on Windows npx opens an extra cmd.exe. The wrapper also decides which Chrome to attach to (see the top of that file).
